# mcx-arduino-core

> Arduino board support package (an Arduino core) for NXP's FRDM-MCXA153, FRDM-MCXN947, FRDM-MCXA156, FRDM-MCXN236 and FRDM-MCXC444 boards. Sketches use the standard Arduino API. The documents below say what is supported, and on which pins, for each board.

Points to keep in mind when writing a sketch for this core:

- Install it from the Arduino IDE's Boards Manager with the URL `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teddokano/mcx-arduino-core/main/package_nxp_mcx_index.json`. The board IDs (FQBNs) are `nxp:mcx:frdm_mcxa153`, `nxp:mcx:frdm_mcxn947`, `nxp:mcx:frdm_mcxa156`, `nxp:mcx:frdm_mcxn236` and `nxp:mcx:frdm_mcxc444`.
- The boards are ARM Cortex-M (Cortex-M33; Cortex-M0+ on FRDM-MCXC444), not AVR. AVR registers and libraries written only for AVR do not work. `<avr/pgmspace.h>` and `PROGMEM` are provided so that code using them builds.
- Instance names other than `Serial`, `Wire` and `SPI` (`Serial1`, `Serial2`, `Wire1`, `Wire2`, `SPI1`) mean different pins on each board, and some boards do not have them. Check "Instance names by board" in API_COMPATIBILITY.md first.
- Which pins have PWM (`analogWrite()`) and analog input (`analogRead()`) differs by board. Check the board's pin mapping.
- A shield whose I2C is on `A4`/`A5` (UNO R3 style) needs `Wire.setPins(A4, A5)` before `Wire.begin()`. It works on FRDM-MCXA156, FRDM-MCXN236 and FRDM-MCXC444, and returns `false` on FRDM-MCXA153 and FRDM-MCXN947, whose `A4`/`A5` have no I2C.
- Ethernet: on FRDM-MCXN947, the bundled `MCXEthernet` library (`#include <MCXEthernet.h>`, with the same classes as the official Ethernet library) uses the on-board port. On any of the boards, the official `Ethernet` library works with a W5500 module.
- `Servo` and `EEPROM` are bundled, with the same API as the official libraries, and so are `MsTimer2` and `TimerOne`, with the API of the AVR libraries of those names (`TimerOne` without its PWM functions: use `analogWrite()` and `analogWriteFrequency()`). `mcxTicker` has the API of the ESP32/ESP8266 cores' `Ticker` under that class name (`#include <mcxTicker.h>`, `mcxTicker t; t.attach_ms(500, f);`), for any number of functions, in whole milliseconds.

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teddokano/mcx-arduino-core/main/README.md): supported boards, installation, and an overview of the package
- [Tutorial](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teddokano/mcx-arduino-core/main/TUTORIAL.md): from installation to the first sketches, step by step
- [API compatibility](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teddokano/mcx-arduino-core/main/API_COMPATIBILITY.md): every Arduino API and its status on each board, instance names by board, and what is not supported
- [Pin mapping: FRDM-MCXA153](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teddokano/mcx-arduino-core/main/PIN_MAPPING_A153.md)
- [Pin mapping: FRDM-MCXN947](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teddokano/mcx-arduino-core/main/PIN_MAPPING_N947.md)
- [Pin mapping: FRDM-MCXA156](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teddokano/mcx-arduino-core/main/PIN_MAPPING_A156.md): the board needs resistor changes, described here
- [Pin mapping: FRDM-MCXN236](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teddokano/mcx-arduino-core/main/PIN_MAPPING_N236.md): the board needs resistor changes, described here
- [Pin mapping: FRDM-MCXC444](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teddokano/mcx-arduino-core/main/PIN_MAPPING_C444.md)

## Bundled libraries

- [MCXEthernet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teddokano/mcx-arduino-core/main/hardware/nxp/mcx/libraries/MCXEthernet/README.md): Ethernet on FRDM-MCXN947's on-board port, with the official Ethernet library's API
- [mcxPinState](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teddokano/mcx-arduino-core/main/docs/mcxpinstate_guide.md): shows which peripheral owns each pin, for debugging
- [mcxRCServo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teddokano/mcx-arduino-core/main/hardware/nxp/mcx/libraries/mcxRCServo/README.md): hobby RC servos from the PWM pins
